I hadn't realized that @jsturtevant had already set the milestone. That probably should have been done last, right? Where can I read up on managing milestones?

@pohly That's kind of correct. However, the milestone can be set only after Release Team Leads approve an exception for the PR to get merged. I'm not sure if we have this somewhere else documented, but this document has some basic information about the process (it's more oriented towards SIG Release members though): https://github.com/kubernetes/sig-release/blob/master/releases/release_phases.md

> We passed test freeze, does this qualify to merge at this stage? @kubernetes/release-managers @liggitt do you know?

I don't have context on the issue this is fixing, but in general, test-only fixes for flakes and failing tests that improve signal for release, whether in release-blocking or release-informing jobs, are ~always acceptable.

The test freeze deadline is more about expanding test coverage, or adding new tests, if I understand correctly.

> > We passed test freeze, does this qualify to merge at this stage? @kubernetes/release-managers @liggitt do you know?
> 
> I don't have context on the issue this is fixing, but in general, test-only fixes for flakes and failing tests that improve signal for release, whether in release-blocking or release-informing jobs, are ~always acceptable.
> 
> The test freeze deadline is more about expanding test coverage, or adding new tests, if I understand correctly.

The problem I see is _how_ the PR got merged, not the end result. Having an additional pair of eyes from the release team would raise the general awareness about a merge, which has been an issue in previous release cycles. 

Especially when the process is well defined, but maybe we should improve there.
I moved the discussion to https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C2C40FMNF/p1700057962137919 because it's more about the process and less about this particular PR.

> This could be improved further, as discussed in this PR. I assume that @jsturtevant will remember that in a personal TODO list and might come back to it when there's no test freeze looming. We don't need to record such a TODO here or in an issue because it could also remain as-is.

review_comments:
The purpose of these log messages apparently was to have this information available in case of a test failure.

What I had in mind was something like this:
```
type state struct {
    replicas int
    as ...
}

framework.Gomega().Consistently(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) result {
...
})....Should(gomega.HaveField("replicas", omega.And(gomega.BeNumerically(">=", minDesiredReplicas), gomega.BeNumerically("<=", maxDesiredReplicas))))
```

Then when it fails, gomega dumps the entire state as part of the failure message. But the usability of that failure would have to be tested.

For now, keep this is as-is and add a `framework.ExpectNoError(err)` after it to check the result of `Consistently`.

I put this at the end of the test so that we can dump the HPA Status
Right, that was the idea.
This returns an error that would need to returned by `EnsureDesiredReplicasInRange`. As you are not doing that yet, capture it in `err` and check it below.
